Fix xmlOutputBufferGetContent output when encoder is set.

The xmlOutputBufferGetContent function only returns the buffer attribute
of the _xmlOutputBuffer struct.

emptied. This causes the xmlOutputBufferGetContent to always return

encoder is set.

uri: fix signed integer overflow in xmlBuildRelativeURISafe

This patch changes the types of ix, nbslash, len, and pos from int to
size_t in xmlBuildRelativeURISafe. These variables are used to index
and measure path strings that can exceed INT_MAX bytes (~2.14 GB),
causing two independent signed integer overflow vulnerabilities.

1. The loop counter ix can overflow from INT_MAX to INT_MIN when
   traversing a base path longer than INT_MAX bytes, leading to an
   out-of-bounds read (CWE-125).

2. The expression 3 * nbslash in the xmlMalloc size argument can
   overflow int, resulting in an undersized allocation followed by
   a heap buffer overflow in the write loop (CWE-122).

An overflow check is also added before the xmlMalloc call to handle
the case where the size_t arithmetic would itself overflow.

fault.

Every other xmlMalloc call in schematron.c already has a proper NULL
check. This patch adds the missing check and frees the name, value, and
compiled XPath expression before returning to avoid memory leaks on the
error path.

parser: Pass userData to SAX text callbacks in xmlParseReference

When replaceEntities is on and the entity's cached tree is reused,
the first/last text-child optimization in xmlParseReference called
ctxt->sax->characters / cdataBlock with ctxt as the first argument
instead of ctxt->userData. Every other SAX callsite in parser.c
correctly passes ctxt->userData.

With xmlSchemaSAXPlug installed (as set up by
xmlTextReaderSetSchema / xmlTextReaderSchemaValidate), userData is
a _xmlSchemaSAXPlug*, so handing over a raw ctxt to the registered
charactersSplit handler produces a type-confused dereference:
charactersSplit reads ctxt->myDoc as user_sax and ctxt->myDoc->URL
as user_sax->characters, then calls that string pointer as code.
The result is a reliable SIGSEGV on the first entity reference in
any XSD-validated xmlTextReader stream (and a silent validation
bypass on the rare targets where the confused call doesn't crash).

Fix by passing ctxt->userData, matching the rest of the file.

memory: add xmlGrowArray helper for overflow-checked array reallocation

Add a private helper function that combines xmlGrowCapacity() with
xmlRealloc() into a single call. This reduces boilerplate at array
growth sites where the same pattern of capacity check + realloc +
pointer/capacity update is repeated.

On success, updates the capacity and returns the new pointer.
On failure, returns NULL with the original pointer and capacity
preserved, avoiding the common self-assignment bug where the old
pointer is lost.

relaxng: use xmlGrowArray for overflow-checked array growth

Replace 9 unsafe array growth sites with xmlGrowArray() which provides
overflow-checked capacity growth and safe reallocation. The old code
used unchecked int * 2 multiplication before xmlRealloc which can
overflow on 32-bit systems, and several sites updated the capacity
counter before allocation and used self-assignment, causing state
corruption and memory leaks on allocation failure.

One site (xmlRelaxNGGetElements) uses xmlGrowCapacity directly because
it needs a +1 sentinel element in the allocation.

schematron: use xmlGrowArray for overflow-checked array growth

Replace 2 unsafe array growth sites with xmlGrowArray(). The old code
used unchecked max * 4 * sizeof triple multiplication before xmlRealloc
which can overflow, producing undersized allocations followed by heap
buffer overflows. Both sites also used self-assignment, losing the old
pointer on allocation failure.

- relaxng.c (xmlRelaxNGGetElements): migrate the last in-function

  with the other call sites. Drop the unnecessary "+1" in the malloc

the problem reported

```
c14n.c:2171: error: Reached end of file while still searching closing
'`' of a verbatim block starting at line 2062 (warning treated as
error, aborting now)
```

See https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/commit/e549622bc5b93631c9ee00d94afec533ecd467c7#note_2833189

regexp: Only set error on first failure

Problematic regular expressions may fail early during compilation.
In that case, only log the error once to avoid misleading messages.
